copy.en:
Is a whale really a fish?

Nope! Even though whales live in the sea, they're mammals like us — they breathe air, feed milk to their babies, and even use air inside to make their songs!
copy.tl:
Isda ba talaga ang balyena?

Hindi pala! Kahit nakatira sa dagat ang balyena, mamalya sila tulad natin—humihinga sila ng hangin, nagpapasuso ng anak, at gumagamit pa ng hangin sa loob para kumanta!
copy.bis:
Isda ba gyud ang balyena?

Dili diay! Bisan nagpuyo sa dagat ang balyena, mammal sila sama nato—naginhawa sila og hangin, nagpasuso sa ilang anak, ug mogamit pa og hangin sa sulod aron mokanta!

copy.bis: Naay mga balyena ug dolphin nga nagpuyo sa Tañon Strait, ang tubig taliwala sa Cebu ug Negros. Protektado kini nga dapit busa luwas sila nga makakanta ug makalangoy didto.

copy.tl: Ang wave ay isang disturbance na kumakalat mula sa pinagmulan, parang mga alon na lumalaganap sa palanggana kapag tinapik mo ang tubig.
copy.bis: Ang wave kay usa ka disturbance nga mokatap palayo sa tinubdan, sama sa mga balod nga mikatap sa planggana kon imong tapikon ang tubig.

copy.en: A salt is a neutral ionic compound, which means it is made of charged particles that balance each other out, and it is produced when an acid and a base react.
copy.tl: Ang asin ay isang neutral ionic compound, ibig sabihin ito ay gawa sa mga charged particles na nagbabalanse sa isa't isa, at ito ay nabubuo kapag nag-react ang acid at base.
copy.bis: Ang asin kay usa ka neutral ionic compound, nagpasabot nga kini hinimo sa mga charged particles nga nagbalanse sa usag usa, ug kini maporma kon mo-react ang acid ug base.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: freeze, and grow bigger before falling

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover

copy.en: Hail is balls of ice! Raindrops get carried up into the super cold parts of a tall thundercloud, freeze, and grow bigger before falling. It's rare in the Philippines because our climate is warm!
copy.tl: Ang hail ay mga bilog na yelo! Patak ng ulan ang naitataas sa napakalamig na bahagi ng makapal na ulap, nagyeyelo at lumalaki bago bumagsak. Bihira sa Pilipinas dahil mainit ang klima!
copy.bis: Ang hail mao ang lingin nga yelo! Tulo sa ulan ang madala pataas sa hilabihan kabugnaw nga bahin sa baga nga panganod, mag-yelo ug modako una mahulog. Talagsa sa Pilipinas tungod kay init ang klima!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity as the cause of an orbit but does not teach gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth in predictable ways. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An orbit is the curved path an object follows as it goes around another object in space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an orbit but does not discuss Earth's tilt, intensity of sunlight, or seasonal changes, nor does it involve making a model or drawings. It is only background vocabulary for the competency.

copy.en:
What is an orbit?

An orbit is the curved path an object follows as it goes around another object in space, held in by gravity—like a satellite circling Earth!
copy.tl:
Ano ang orbit?

Ang orbit ay ang paikot na landas na sinusundan ng isang bagay habang umiikot ito sa palibot ng isa pang bagay sa kalawakan, na hinihila ng gravity—tulad ng satellite na umiikot sa Earth!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang orbit?

Ang orbit mao ang likoanan nga agianan nga ginasunod sa usa ka butang samtang naglibot kini sa laing butang sa kawanangan, nga gibira sa grabidad—sama sa satellite nga naglibot sa Earth!

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains weathering as the breaking of rocks into smaller pieces, which is a precursor to soil formation, but it does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It provides background knowledge rather than directly teaching the competency.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses rock breakdown but does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting different types of rocks, nor describing similarities and differences in features such as texture, color, or grain crystal size. It shares the topic of rocks but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How do giant rocks break into smaller pieces?

Through weathering! Heat, cold, water, and wind slowly break large rocks into smaller pieces over time.
copy.tl:
Paano nababasag ang mga malalaking bato sa mas maliliit na piraso?

Sa weathering! Ang init, lamig, tubig, at hangin ay unti-unting nagdurog sa malalaking bato tungo sa mas maliliit na piraso.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkabuak ang dagkong bato ngadto sa gagmay nga piraso?

Pinaagi sa weathering! Ang init, bugnaw, tubig, ug hangin hinay-hinay nga nagkadugmok sa dagkong bato ngadto sa gagmay nga piraso.

copy.bis: Ang non-porous nga mga materyales dili magpaagi sa hangin o liquid, sama sa plastic ruler nga magpabilin nga uga sa tubig.

copy.en:
How is a wheel and axle different from a regular lever?

A wheel and axle is like a continuously turning lever! Instead of one push stroke, you can push round and round without stopping. The center of the axle acts as the fulcrum.
copy.tl:
Paano naiiba ang wheel and axle sa isang ordinaryong lever?

Ang wheel and axle ay parang lever na patuloy na umiikot! Sa halip na isang tulak lang, paikot-ikot kang makakatulak nang walang hinto. Ang sentro ng ehe ang nagsisilbing fulcrum.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa wheel and axle sa ordinaryong lever?

Ang wheel and axle sama sa lever nga padayon nga nagtuyok! Imbes usa ra ka duso, makaduso ka libot-libot nga walay hunong. Ang tunga sa ehe mao ang nagsilbing fulcrum.

copy.en:
How was the very first wheel used?

Made 5,500 years ago in Mesopotamia, it’s one of the oldest inventions! It was first used for shaping pottery, not carts!
copy.tl:
Paano ginamit ang pinakaunang gulong?

Ginawa 5,500 years ago sa Mesopotamia, ito isa sa pinakamatandang imbensiyon! Ginamit muna ito sa paggawa ng palayok, hindi sa kareton!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit ang una nga ligid?

Gihimo 5,500 years ago sa Mesopotamia, kini usa sa pinakakaraang imbensiyon! Una kini gigamit sa paghimo og kolon, dili sa mga karetilya!

copy.en: Did you know the dwarf planet Pluto was first discovered way back in the year 1930? It has been hiding in space for a long time!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na ang dwarf planet na Pluto ay natuklasan noong taong 1930? Matagal na siyang nakatago sa kalawakan!
copy.bis: Nahibalo ba ka nga ang dwarf planet nga Pluto nadiskobre niadtong tuig 1930? Dugay na siyang nagtago sa kalawakan!

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram; it is about animal behavior, not habitat classification.

copy.en: Knowing why animals behave the way they do helps us work with them better — like a farmer knowing when a carabao won't overheat, or training dogs to search and guard.
copy.tl: Kapag naiintindihan natin kung bakit ganoon kumilos ang hayop, mas maayo natin silang magagamit — gaya ng alam ng magsasaka kung kailan di-naiinitan ang kalabaw, o pagsasanay ng aso para tumulong maghanap at magbantay.
copy.bis: Kon masabtan nato kung ngano molihok sa ingon ang mananap, mas maayo nato silang magamit — sama sa nahibaloan sa mag-uuma kung kanus-a dili mainit ang kabaw, o pagbansay sa iro aron motabang mangita ug mobantay.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why atoms bond (lower energy/stability) but does not address that bond formation/breaking constitutes a chemical change or the formation of a new substance, which is the core of G9-M-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Atoms bond together because they have lower energy when they team up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses bonding in general but never mentions valence electrons, the outer shell, or their role in bond formation, so it does not directly support G9-M-3.

copy.en: Atoms bond together because they have lower energy when they team up! Being together makes them much more stable than being separated.
copy.tl: Nagbi-bond ang mga atomo dahil mas mababa ang energy nila kapag nagtutulungan! Mas stable sila kapag magkasama kaysa kapag hiwa-hiwalay.
copy.bis: Mag-bond ang mga atomo tungod kay mas ubos ang energy nila kon magtinabangay! Mas malig-on sila kon magkauban kaysa kon magbulag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yeast, a tiny fungus
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions yeast is a fungus, which is one of the microorganisms named in the competency, but it does not use a table or classify living things into groups. The card's focus is on why bread rises, not on classification. The format-required table is absent, so it cannot directly support G5-L-4.

copy.en:
Why does bread rise?

Yeast, a tiny fungus, eats sugar in the dough and gives off carbon-dioxide gas — the gas bubbles puff up the bread!
copy.tl:
Bakit umaalsa ang tinapay?

Kumakain ng asukal ang lebadura (yeast), isang napakaliit na fungus, at naglalabas ito ng carbon-dioxide gas — ang mga bulang ito ang nagpapalobo sa tinapay!
copy.bis:
Nganong moalsa ang pan?

Ang lebadura (yeast), usa ka gamayng fungus, mokaon og asukar ug mobuga og carbon-dioxide gas — kining mga bula ang naghubag sa pan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a species goes extinct, it's gone forever — it can never come back.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that extinction is permanent and affects nature, but does not address threats to biodiversity or how those threats lead to extinction, nor does it involve a class discussion as required by the format.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Other plants and animals feel it too, since everything in nature is connected.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions interconnectedness but does not explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem stability during difficult conditions such as food shortages, disease, or climate change.

copy.en: When a species goes extinct, it's gone forever — it can never come back. Other plants and animals feel it too, since everything in nature is connected.
copy.tl: Kapag naubos na ang isang species, permanente na ito at hindi na maibabalik. Naaapektuhan din ang ibang hayop at halaman dahil magkakaugnay sila sa ekosistema.
copy.bis: Kung mahurot na ang usa ka species, permanente na kini ug dili na mabalik. Maapektohan usab ang ubang hayop ug tanom kay magkadugtong sila sa ekosistema.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hair's color-making cells stop producing melanin as we age
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses hair color and aging, not the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It only tangentially involves a living process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hair's color-making cells stop producing melanin as we age
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cells but does not use a labelled diagram or describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere.

copy.en:
Why does hair turn gray as we age?

Hair's color-making cells stop producing melanin as we age, so new hair grows in without color — turning gray or white.
copy.tl:
Bakit umuubanin ang buhok kapag tumatanda?

Tumitigil ang mga selula sa paggawa ng melanin, ang pigment na nagbibigay-kulay sa buhok, kaya tumutubo na itong walang kulay — nagiging puti o uban.
copy.bis:
Nganong mangubanon ang buhok kon magkatigulang?

Mohunong ang mga selula sa paghimo og melanin, ang pigment nga maghatag og kolor sa buhok, busa moturok kini nga walay kolor — mahimong puti o ubanon.

copy.en: Intensity scales help scientists assess earthquake effects, compare earthquakes, assess risk, raise public awareness, and support scientific research for preparedness.
copy.tl: Ang intensity scales ay tumutulong sa mga scientist na suriin ang epekto ng lindol, ikumpara ang mga lindol, tasahin ang panganib, itaas ang kamalayan ng publiko, at suportahan ang siyentipikong pananaliksik para sa paghahanda.
copy.bis: Ang intensity scales makatabang sa mga scientist sa pagsusi sa epekto sa linog, pagtandi sa mga linog, pagtasa sa peligro, pagpataas sa kahibalo sa publiko, ug pagsuporta sa siyentipikong panukiduki para sa pagpangandam.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In complete metamorphosis, the larva and the adult eat totally different foods
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions complete metamorphosis and different foods of larva and adult, but does not use a flow chart to compare life-cycle stages as required by the competency. It does not directly support the skill of comparing stages via flow charts; it only touches on a related fact about butterfly life stages.

copy.en:
Why don't a caterpillar and a butterfly compete for food?

In complete metamorphosis, the larva and the adult eat totally different foods — so they never have to compete for the same meal!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi nag-aagawan ng pagkain ang uod at paru-paro?

Sa ganap na metamorphosis, magkaiba ang kinakain ng larva at ng hingkod na hayop — kaya hindi sila nag-aagawan ng pagkain!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili mag-indigay sa pagkaon ang ulod ug alibangbang?

Sa kompleto nga metamorphosis, lahi ang kaonon sa larva ug sa hamtong nga hayop — mao nga dili sila mag-indigay sa pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most ocean waves are made by wind pushing on the water's surface!

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that wind pushes water to create waves, which is an example of a natural cause moving water. It only touches on one specific phenomenon without supporting the broader skill of exploring/demonstrating ways to move objects.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how wind creates ocean waves, but it does not identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver. assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions yeast, a microorganism, but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). It provides no classification instruction or table, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: To test if yeast is alive, mix it with warm water and a little sugar — if it bubbles and foams up in minutes, it's ready to bake!
copy.tl: Para malaman kung buhay pa ang yeast, ihalo ito sa maligamgam na tubig at kaunting asukal — kung bumubula at umuusbong sa ilang minuto, handa na itong gamitin!
copy.bis: Aron mahibaloan kung buhi pa ang yeast, isagol kini sa init-init nga tubig ug gamayng asukal — kung mobula ug mosaka sulod sa pipila ka minuto, andam na kini gamiton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yeast belongs to the fungi group, along with mushrooms and mold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that yeast is a fungus, but it does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups, nor does it cover the broader classification of plants, animals, and microorganisms. It only touches on one group (fungi) without the required table format or comparative characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yeast belongs to the fungi group, along with mushrooms and mold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fungi as a group but does not describe the importance of the six-kingdom or three-domain systems of classification. It provides a single fact about yeast's classification, not an explanation of classification systems.

copy.en:
Is yeast a plant?

Nope! Yeast belongs to the fungi group, along with mushrooms and mold — it's neither a plant nor an animal, but its own kind of living thing.
copy.tl:
Halaman ba ang lebadura?

Hindi pala! Ang lebadura ay kabilang sa grupo ng fungi, kasama ang kabute at amag — hindi ito halaman ni hayop, kundi natatanging uri ng nabubuhay.
copy.bis:
Tanom ba ang lebadura?

Dili diay! Ang lebadura sakop sa grupo sa fungi, kauban sa uhong ug agup-op — dili kini tanom ni hayop, kondili linaing matang sa buhing butang.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions metals as conductors but provides no information about subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons), their symbols, masses, charges, or locations within an atom.

copy.en: Zinc and iron are electrical conductors used as parts of electrical and electronic devices.
copy.tl: Ang zinc at bakal ay mga electrical conductors na ginagamit bilang bahagi ng mga electrical at electronic devices.
copy.bis: Ang zinc ug puthaw mga electrical conductors nga gigamit isip mga parte sa electrical ug electronic devices.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Zinc is a mineral your body needs to grow, fight sickness, and heal wounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses zinc as a nutrient/mineral and its general functions; it does not trace food through the digestive tract, use a labeled diagram, or explain digestive processes such as mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, or elimination.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: found in foods like oysters, meat, and fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food as a source of zinc but does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) or teach that these are basic needs. The food reference is only incidental vocabulary overlap.

copy.en:
What does zinc do for your body?

Zinc is a mineral your body needs to grow, fight sickness, and heal wounds — found in foods like oysters, meat, and fish.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng zinc sa katawan?

Ang zinc ay mineral na kailangan ng katawan para lumaki, labanan ang sakit, at pagalingin ang sugat — makukuha sa talaba, karne, at isda.
copy.bis:
Unsay buhaton sa zinc sa lawas?

Ang zinc mineral nga gikinahanglan sa lawas aron motubo, makig-away sa sakit, ug maayo ang samad — makuha sa talaba, karne, ug isda.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the Sun seems to pass through each one over a year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Sun's apparent path through zodiac constellations over a year, which touches on the idea of changing star patterns, but it does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, nor does it explain seasons, star patterns, or eclipses as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so they're called 'zodiac signs'!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions zodiac constellations and the Sun's apparent path, which is related to constellations, but it does not explain why ancient cultures relied on constellations for direction or season verification. It only states a modern astronomical fact without historical or cultural context.

copy.en: The zodiac has 12 constellations along the ecliptic—the Sun's apparent path across the sky. As Earth orbits, the Sun seems to pass through each one over a year, so they're called 'zodiac signs'!
copy.tl: Ang zodiac ay may 12 konstelasyon sa kahabaan ng ecliptic—ang tila landas ng Araw sa kalangitan. Habang umiikot ang Earth, tila dumadaan ang Araw sa bawat isa sa loob ng isang taon, kaya 'zodiac signs' ang tawag!
copy.bis: Ang zodiac adunay 12 ka konstelasyon sa kahabaan sa ecliptic—ang daw nga dalan sa Adlaw sa kalangitan. Samtang naglibot ang Yuta, daw moagi ang Adlaw sa matag usa sulod sa usa ka tuig, mao nga 'zodiac signs' ang tawag!

copy.en: Abaca fiber comes from the thick leaf stalks that form the plant's trunk-like stem.
copy.tl: Ang hibla ng abaka ay nakukuha sa makapal na tangkay ng dahon na bumubuo sa parang-puno ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang lanot sa abaka ginakuha gikan sa baga nga tangkay sa dahon nga maoy nahimong morag puno sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: leaf stalks that make up the plant's trunk-like stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card names leaf stalks and a trunk-like stem but does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only identifies a plant part as a fiber source, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: leaf stalks that make up the plant's trunk-like stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shoot-system parts (leaf stalks, trunk-like stem) but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important. The content is about abaca fiber origin, not plant system function.

copy.en: Abaca fiber comes from the outer layers of leaf stalks that make up the plant's trunk-like stem.
copy.tl: Ang hibla ng abaka ay kinukuha sa balat ng mga tangkay ng dahon na bumubuo sa parang-punong katawan nito.
copy.bis: Ang hilo sa abaka gikuha gikan sa gawas nga panit sa mga tangkay sa dahon nga naghimo sa iyang murag-puno nga lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Abaca is also made into bags, mats, and various handicrafts that Filipinos sell.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G3-E-2 is specifically about useful things made from non-living materials. Abaca is a plant fiber, a living material, so the card does not support the competency and is unrelated to its intended subject.

copy.en: Abaca is also made into bags, mats, and various handicrafts that Filipinos sell.
copy.tl: Mula sa abaka ay gumagawa rin ng mga bag, banig, at iba't ibang handicraft na ibinebenta ng mga Pilipino.
copy.bis: Gikan sa abaka gihimo usab ang mga bag, banig, ug lain-laing handicraft nga gibaligya sa mga Pilipino.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the abaniko moves the air! This air carries heat and sweat away from your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes moving air carrying heat away, which is a convection-related phenomenon, but it never names conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it identify advantageous/disadvantageous examples of these heat transfer modes. It only provides a common everyday effect without linking it to the specific competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This air carries heat and sweat away from your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sweat being carried away, which implies evaporation (a change of state), but it does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes. It does not discuss melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation, nor the heat energy involved. The mention of sweat is incidental and not developed into an explanation of state change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This air carries heat and sweat away from your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It only mentions sweat being carried away, which is a hint of evaporation, but there is no description of temperature-driven state changes. The content is about cooling via air movement, not about state changes of matter.

copy.en:
Why do we feel cooler when using an abaniko?

When you wave it, the abaniko moves the air! This air carries heat and sweat away from your skin, making you feel much cooler.
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nagiging mas malamig kapag gumagamit ng abaniko?

Kapag pinapaypay mo, pinapagalaw ng abaniko ang hangin! Dinala ng hangin ang init at pawis palayo sa balat mo, kaya mas nakakaramdam ka ng lamig.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas bugnaw ang atong gibati kon magpaypay ta ug abaniko?

Kon paypayon nimo, gipalihok sa abaniko ang hangin! Gidala sa hangin ang init ug singot palayo sa panit, mao nga mas bugnaw ang imong gibati.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Abrasion breaks rocks as fragments rub against each other in moving water like streams and rivers.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes rock abrasion/erosion in moving water, an earth-science process. It does not explore or demonstrate ways to make objects move by natural causes such as wind and water; it only mentions moving water as the setting for rock breakage, not object movement.

copy.en: Abrasion breaks rocks as fragments rub against each other in moving water like streams and rivers.
copy.tl: Ang abrasion ay nagbabasag ng mga bato habang ang mga piraso nito ay nagkikiskisan sa isa't isa sa umaagos na tubig tulad ng mga sapa at ilog.
copy.bis: Ang abrasion nagabuak sa mga bato samtang ang mga piraso nagkuskos sa usag usa sa nagdagayday nga tubig sama sa mga sapa ug suba.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind carrying sand slowly scrapes and wears down rocks close to the ground
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wind abrasion (wearing down rocks), which is a weathering/erosion process, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. The focus is on scraping and wearing down, not on the movement/transport of materials from one place to another. Thus it only shares the broad topic of erosion without directly supporting the transport aspect of the competency.

copy.en:
How does wind act like sandpaper on rocks?

Wind carrying sand slowly scrapes and wears down rocks close to the ground, just like sandpaper!
copy.tl:
Paano gumagalaw ang hangin na parang sandpaper sa mga bato?

Ang hangin na may dalang buhangin ay unti-unting kumukuskos at nag-uukit sa mga bato malapit sa lupa, parang sandpaper!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglihok sa hangin nga murag sandpaper sa mga bato?

Ang hangin nga nagdala ug balas hinay-hinay nga nagkuskos ug nagbanlas sa mga bato duol sa yuta, sama sa sandpaper!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that power-plant generators produce AC, the type used in home outlets. It does not describe high voltage generation, safe distribution to industries/businesses/homes, or the roles of substations and electric meters, which are the core actions of G10-F-9.

copy.en: Most large power-plant generators make alternating current or AC, which is the exact kind of electricity flowing in your home outlets!
copy.tl: Karamihan sa malalaking generator sa power plant ay gumagawa ng alternating current o AC, ang kuryenteng dumadaloy sa mga saksak ng bahay!
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa dagkong generator sa power plant naghimo ug alternating current o AC, ang kuryenteng moagas sa mga outlet sa balay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acceleration is any change in speed or direction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate in practical situations and describe that acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction as the result of a net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines acceleration as a change in speed or direction and gives practical examples (speeding up, slowing down, turning), but it omits the essential causal condition 'as the result of a net force' that is part of the competency. It does not teach the net-force relationship, so it only shares the vocabulary/definition without directly supporting the full competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acceleration is any change in speed or direction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires identifying that forces cause acceleration and that acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. The card only states that acceleration is a change in speed or direction; it does not mention force, velocity, or rate of change. It provides a simplified definition but does not directly support the competency's core concepts.

copy.en: Acceleration is any change in speed or direction! It happens when a vehicle speeds up, slows down, or turns.
copy.tl: Ang aselerasyon ay pagbabago sa bilis o direksyon! Nangyayari ito kapag bumibilis, bumabagal, o lumiliko ang sasakyan.
copy.bis: Ang aselerasyon mao ang pagbag-o sa katulin o direksyon! Mahitabo kini kon mopaspas, mohinay, o moliko ang sakyanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acetone is an organic compound commonly used as a cleaner
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes acetone as a cleaner for nail polish, which is unrelated to making a simple electromagnet and observing its properties. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Acetone is an organic compound commonly used as a cleaner, especially for removing nail polish.
copy.tl: Ang acetone ay isang organic compound na karaniwang ginagamit bilang panlinis, lalo na sa pagtanggal ng nail polish.
copy.bis: Ang acetone usa ka organic compound nga sagad gigamit isip panglimpyo, ilabi na sa pagtangtang sa nail polish.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sour things like vinegar and calamansi juice are acids! Meanwhile, soap and baking soda are bases

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sour things like vinegar and calamansi juice are acids! Meanwhile, soap and baking soda are bases

assignedReviews.reason: The card names common household acids and bases, but it does not use any indicator, nor does it identify salts or use the indicator-based identification required by the competency. It provides background examples only.

copy.en: Sour things like vinegar and calamansi juice are acids! Meanwhile, soap and baking soda are bases—they feel slippery and taste bitter.
copy.tl: Ang mga maasim tulad ng suka at katas ng calamansi ay acids! Samantala, ang sabon at baking soda ay bases—madulas at mapait.
copy.bis: Ang mga aslom sama sa suka ug duga sa calamansi mga acids! Samtang, ang sabon ug baking soda mga bases—danlog ug pait.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: HCl is a strong acid even when diluted because it fully ionizes, while vinegar is weak even when concentrated.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses acid strength vs concentration and mentions HCl and vinegar, but does not address identifying solutions as acids, bases, or salts using litmus indicator, which is the core of G7-M-11.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: HCl is a strong acid even when diluted because it fully ionizes, while vinegar is weak even when concentrated.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions common acids (HCl, vinegar) but does not teach identifying acids, bases, or salts using indicators. It focuses on the distinction between strength and concentration, not identification with indicators.

copy.en:
Is a strong acid always concentrated?

No! Acid strength and concentration differ. HCl is a strong acid even when diluted because it fully ionizes, while vinegar is weak even when concentrated.
copy.tl:
Ang malakas na acid ba ay laging concentrated?

Hindi! Magkaiba ang strength at concentration. Ang HCl ay malakas kahit diluted dahil fully ionizes ito, habang ang suka ay mahina kahit concentrated.
copy.bis:
Ang kusog nga acid ba kanunay nga concentrated?

Dili! Lahi ang strength ug concentration. Ang HCl kusog bisan diluted kay hingpit kining nagiionize, samtang ang suka mahuyang bisan concentrated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acids usually taste sour, while bases taste bitter and feel slippery!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts

assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires identifying common acids, bases, and salts using different indicators. copy.en: Acids usually taste sour, while bases taste bitter and feel slippery!
copy.tl: Ang mga asido ay karaniwang maasim, habang ang mga base ay mapait at madulas!
copy.bis: Ang mga asido kasagaran aslom, samtang ang mga base mapait ug danlog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an acid and a base react, they neutralize each other!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions acids, bases, and salts but does not address identifying solutions using litmus indicator or finding them at home/school. It only describes the neutralization reaction, which is not the skill in this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an acid and a base react, they neutralize each other!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe important types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement)
assignedReviews.reason: Neutralization is a specific acid-base reaction, but the competency requires describing combination, decomposition, single replacement, and double replacement reactions. The card does not describe these general types or classify neutralization within them.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This cool reaction usually forms a salt and water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions acids, bases, and salts, but the competency requires identifying common acids, bases, and salts using indicators. The card does not name any common substances or discuss indicators, so it does not directly support identification.

copy.en: When an acid and a base react, they neutralize each other! This cool reaction usually forms a salt and water.
copy.tl: Kapag nag-react ang isang acid at isang base, nag-neneutralize sila sa isa't isa! Karaniwan, nakakagawa sila ng isang salt at tubig.
copy.bis: Kung mag-react ang usa ka acid ug usa ka base, mag-neutralize sila sa usag usa! Kasagaran, makahimo sila og salt ug tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Strong ones like muriatic acid and lye are dangerous.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions muriatic acid and lye as examples of strong acids/bases, but it does not teach identifying solutions using litmus indicator or classifying them as acids, bases, and salts. The focus is safety/harm, not identification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Strong ones like muriatic acid and lye are dangerous.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card names common strong acid/base examples but does not teach identifying common acids, bases, and salts using indicators. It only warns about their danger, so it does not directly support the identification skill.

copy.en:
Are all acids and bases safe to touch?

No! Strong ones like muriatic acid and lye are dangerous. They can burn skin and eyes, so always handle them carefully with protection!
copy.tl:
Ligtas bang hawakan ang lahat ng acid at base?

Hindi! Ang malalakas tulad ng muriatic acid at lye ay mapanganib. Nakakapaso ito sa balat at mata, kaya dapat maingat at may proteksyon!
copy.bis:
Luwas ba ang tanan nga acid ug base nga hawkan?

Dili! Ang kusgan sama sa muriatic acid ug lye delikado. Makapaso kini sa panit ug mata, busa kinahanglang amping ug naay proteksyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Acids can react with metals and slowly wear them away, breaking them down bit by bit!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about acids reacting with metals, but the competency requires explaining how this reaction relates to or impacts the natural and built environments using secondary sources. copy.en: Acids can react with metals and slowly wear them away, breaking them down bit by bit!
copy.tl: Ang mga asido ay maaaring tumugon sa metal at unti-unting sirain ito nang dahan-dahan!
copy.bis: Ang mga asido makareaksyon sa metal ug hinay-hinay nga modaot niini gamay sa gamay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Did you know acids usually taste super sour?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that acids taste sour and gives everyday examples (calamansi, vinegar). It does not address identifying solutions, litmus indicator reactions, or distinguishing acids, bases, and salts as required by the competency.

copy.en: Did you know acids usually taste super sour? You can find this yummy sourness in everyday things like calamansi and vinegar!
copy.tl: Alam mo bang karaniwang maasim ang lasa ng mga asido? Makikita mo ang asim na ito sa kalamansi at suka!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga kasagaran maaslom ang lami sa mga asido? Makita nimo ang aslom niini sa kalamansi ug suka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Activation energy breaks the bonds between reacting molecules
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses activation energy and bond breaking in chemical reactions generally, but does not describe photosynthesis or respiration, nor their raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: allowing atoms to rearrange and form new products
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that chemical equations demonstrate a rearrangement of atoms but the total mass of the system remains the same during a chemical reaction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions atoms rearranging to form new products, which is related to the rearrangement of atoms in chemical reactions, but it does not address chemical equations or conservation of mass, which are the core of this competency.

copy.en: Activation energy breaks the bonds between reacting molecules, allowing atoms to rearrange and form new products.
copy.tl: Sinisira ng activation energy ang mga bonds sa pagitan ng mga reacting molecule, kaya nakakapag-rearrange ang mga atom at nakakabuo ng bagong products.
copy.bis: Gibuak sa activation energy ang mga bonds tali sa mga reacting molecule, mao nga maka-rearrange ang mga atom ug makahimo og bag-ong products.
